name: Meta Fort Worth

research_updates.title: Identity, boundary and chronology
research_updates.notes: Meta broke ground in 2015 and reports the Fort Worth campus operational since 2017; continuous construction and TDLR phases extend the chronology through the 2022 FTW4 schedule and a 2023 small retrofit search result. The current assessor address inventory resolves three accounts at 4500 Like Way and zero at 5000, but no source crosswalks the campus to the selected inventory building.

source.title: Building Texas — How Meta invests in jobs, infrastructure and communities across the state
source.notes: Current operator page reports Fort Worth as operational since 2017, a $1.5 billion-plus investment, 1,200 peak skilled-trade workers, 200-plus operational jobs supported once completed, and more than $5.2 million of direct Tarrant-area funding since 2018. The page gives inconsistent grant counts in two sections, so no grant-count observation is retained; statewide jobs, clean-energy capacity and infrastructure claims are also excluded from the Fort Worth account.

research_updates.title: Winner LLC operator crosswalk
research_updates.notes: SEC subsidiary exhibits list Winner LLC under Meta, while TDLR, Fort Worth audit, appraisal and tax-abatement sources connect Winner to 4500 Like Way and the Facebook/Meta project. Company-wide SEC financials were searched but contain no Fort Worth investment, revenue, payroll, tax, utility or community allocation.

source.title: Meta Platforms 2024 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1 — List of Subsidiaries
source.notes: Meta's subsidiary exhibit includes Winner LLC. Together with address-specific TDLR, local audit and tax records, it supports the project-company crosswalk but does not allocate company-wide financial statement amounts to Fort Worth.

research_updates.title: Adjacent QTS boundary exclusion
research_updates.notes: Tarrant agreement, permit, appraisal, operator and archive searches found Winner's proposed 2019 retrofit at 14100 Park Vista, while current QTS material identifies that address as QTS FTW1. TAD now directly identifies Meta personal-property account 14780998 there and links it to Winner real account 42324937, so its 2021-2025 equipment assessments are retained as a company-county boundary exception. No deed or operating crosswalk transfers QTS's physical facility to Meta; QTS power, area and cooling figures remain excluded.

source.notes: Current QTS material identifies its separate Fort Worth campus at 14100 Park Vista Boulevard. This conflicts with treating Winner's 2019 proposed retrofit at that address as a completed Meta phase, so the address is excluded absent a later ownership and operation crosswalk.

research_updates.notes: Corrected by account-level evidence below. The 2024 top-taxpayer roll remains a distinct City-tax-unit aggregate and is not added to account series. Exact Like Way searches, three TAD accounts, three Tarrant collector accounts and three matching Denton collector ...TAR accounts now establish annual values, jurisdiction-specific exemption treatment, paid levies, dates, payers, zero balances and six recipient distributions.

research_updates.title: City incentives, compliance and payments search
research_updates.notes: Fort Worth CSC 46728, CSC 46727, amendments, audit reports, council packets, contracts, check register and FY2025 accounts-payable audit were reopened. The PeopleSoft audit confirms $14,415,465.40 paid to Winner LLC during October 2023-August 2024 with no exception, but it omits voucher, check, invoice, fund, account, purpose and contract coding. The linked FY2024 detail workbook returned HTTP 403/Akamai Access Denied through direct and browser routes. Because neither the amount nor a component is linked to Chapter 380 or tax abatement in the available record, it remains an unresolved AP aggregate rather than an incentive record.

source.title: Property Tax Abatement and Economic Development Program Agreement Review (Winner, LLC)
source.publisher: City of Fort Worth Department of Internal Audit
source.notes: The audit covers 2015-2017 and year one of Winner's agreements. Two independent official-PDF renderings of its image-only Audit Results table confirmed actual construction spending of $784,208,681, Fort Worth construction spending of $74,215,330 and 466,810 commercial square feet. The audit reviewed pay applications, invoices, construction billings, checks and bank statements and verified vendor addresses. The values overlap the wider operator investment total and do not establish wages, worker residence, vendor ownership or an additive project total.

research_updates.title: County incentive and abatement search
research_updates.notes: Tarrant agreements and schedules establish a conditional ten-year County 60% / Hospital 40% abatement structure; the existing 2018 realized County $1,476,619.34 and Hospital $944,148.72 records remain the only published tax-savings dollars. Account portals now separately show Tarrant-serviced Contract Abatement assessment exemptions for Winner real and personal property from 2018-2025 and no Northwest ISD exemption. Those exemption bases are documented in each assessment record but are not multiplied by generic rates into savings.

source.title: Tarrant County Active Tax Abatements as of March 29, 2023
source.notes: The county schedule reports Winner/Facebook's original $750 million plan, later $500 million, $100 million and $200 million expansions, and actual year-one 2018 county and hospital-district abatements. Later Winner accounts are combined, so their projected and cumulative abatement fields cannot be assigned to a phase or selected building.

research_updates.title: State incentive, exemption and financing search
research_updates.notes: Texas Comptroller records confirm Winner LLC d/b/a Ernst LLC certification from June 22, 2015 through June 22, 2035, establishing eligibility for the qualified-data-center sales/use-tax exemption. Certificate and state transparency routes disclose no annual or cumulative tax-exempt purchase amount or realized state revenue reduction for this campus; no value is imputed from purchases, investment or statewide totals. No TEF, Chapter 313, public-bond or TIF amount was found.

source.title: Texas Comptroller certified data center list
source.notes: The list identifies Winner LLC d/b/a Ernst LLC as a certified data center registered June 22, 2015, with owner, occupant and operator registrations expiring June 22, 2035. Certification establishes eligibility for a state sales-tax exemption but discloses no realized exemption amount.

research_updates.title: Planning, permit and phase search
research_updates.notes: Fort Worth issued-permit reports, development portal, Certificates of Occupancy references, TDLR TABS and archived construction reporting were searched by Winner, Project Ernst, FTW, address, lot and contractor. Four major TDLR estimated-cost observations are retained as source projections without summation; local permits also show later electrical, fire-water and retrofit work but no complete non-overlapping permit ledger or IM3 crosswalk.

research_updates.title: Construction workforce and payroll search
research_updates.notes: Operator, DPR/Fortis contractor, audit, permit, council, workforce-board, QCEW and archive sources were reopened. A mechanical $784,208,681 / 1,200 peak-worker ratio and a 9.46% Fort Worth-spend share were tested and rejected: peak concurrent workers are not job-years or a payroll denominator, construction covers 2015-2017, local spend mixes labor and materials, and phase hours, wages, residence and equipment exclusions are absent. No multiplier satisfies the named-model, vintage, geography and channel-separation requirements.

research_updates.title: Operations employment and payroll search
research_updates.notes: Meta careers, operator posts, incentive agreements, audit compliance, QCEW, CBP, workforce and archive sources were reopened. The greater-than-150 December 2020 people snapshot now supports a low-confidence annual-payroll sensitivity using exactly 150 people and same-vintage Dallas-Fort Worth BLS occupation benchmarks; it is explicitly a conservative scenario anchor, not observed payroll, current headcount, a true-value bound or local household income. The conditional 200-plus jobs-supported projection remains excluded because it may include multiplier channels. Benefits, payroll taxes, bonuses, equity, overtime, contractor margin, occupation mix, hours, residence and retention remain unresolved; induced-employment candidates still fail named-multiplier and double-counting gates.

research_updates.title: Electric utility and grid search
research_updates.notes: Meta energy reports, PUC service-area directories, ERCOT, Oncor, Brazos, AllianceTexas, tariff, substation and council sources were reopened. Multiplying the exact 2020-2024 kWh series by retail-commercial, utility-average or energy-only tariffs was tested and rejected: provider, voltage, rate class, coincident demand, load factor, power factor, riders, taxes, negotiated supply and demand charges are unresolved. The sensitivity would model an arbitrary bill, not campus electricity economics.

research_updates.notes: Fort Worth utility agreements, council records, water and wastewater rates, TWDB, TCEQ, Meta water reports and restoration-benefit reports were searched. Because the orchestrator-owned catalog lacks an actual-withdrawal metric, an exact proposed study.annual_water_withdrawal definition and five proposed reported-actual claim payloads are serialized in the project disposition ledger rather than mislabeled as planned use or inserted into canonical records. No consumption, discharge, reclaimed-water volume, bill or selected-building allocation was found.

research_updates.title: County GDP, employment and wage model dispositions
research_updates.notes: Contract 3.1.0 re-adjudication retains two reproducible but explicitly noncausal 2024 comparisons anchored to the 2017 operating date, with 2009-2016 pre-fit and complete 2009-2024 outcomes; study counties and Tarrant are excluded and eligible donors have 2016 population at 0.35-2.5x Tarrant. Employment uses Multnomah/Miami-Dade/Hidalgo/Gwinnett/Dallas: selected-donor mean pretrend RMSE 0.898884%, equal-weight group RMSE 0.727706%, central gap +6.440928%, and five leave-one-out gaps +4.081297% to +7.856616%; national K=3/K=10 and Texas K=5 extend the design range to +2.698239% to +9.348902%. Nominal weekly wage uses Gwinnett/Norfolk MA/Orange CA/Essex MA/Erie: mean/group RMSE 0.798869%/0.628756%, central +2.306140%, leave-one-out +1.173248% to +3.560600%, and full design range +1.149887% to +3.780752%. Real GDP uses DuPage/Orange CA/Queens/San Diego/Allegheny: mean/group RMSE 1.130872%/0.777872%, national central +11.080969%, leave-one-out +10.254563% to +12.538424%, but Texas-only K=5 is -3.263943%. That +14.344912-point geography swing reverses sign and makes even a single descriptive GDP central value misleading, so the GDP comparison remains an explicit gap rather than a model. Retained gaps are county context, not Meta effects; continuous phases, donor data-center contamination, population/industry differences and pandemic-era shocks prohibit attribution.

research_updates.notes: Direct evidence now also retains the independently rechecked 466,810-square-foot audit actual. A separate low-confidence operations-payroll sensitivity is retained from the observed 2020 people floor and official same-vintage wage benchmarks; it does not convert construction workers, projected jobs supported or selected-building area into payroll. research_updates.title: Metric disposition ledger — fiscal and public costs
research_updates.notes: Corrective account records retain 24 annual account assessments, 48 annual paid-tax subtotals across two collectors and all six recipient distributions. The synthesis aggregates only Winner real/personal Tarrant and Northwest ISD paid claims for each tax year: two components in 2017 and four in 2018-2025; MMI is excluded. The 2025 aggregation defines the equal-cost public-service break-even threshold because actual same-scope marginal costs are unavailable; it is not an observed cost or net result. The 2018 County/Hospital credits reconcile to the same Winner exemption base and tax year and are added once to actual paid tax in a separate gross-before-realized-abatement counterfactual. City CSC 46728 Chapter 380 annual grants, realized state sales-tax exemption dollars and actual marginal public-service costs remain unresolved; the $14,415,465.40 PeopleSoft payee aggregate remains unclassified without atomic coding.

source.title: Tarrant County Tax Abatement Agreement with Winner LLC, Court Order 130032
source.notes: The agreement and application describe a proposed Winner retrofit of an existing data center at 14100 Park Vista Boulevard. Because current QTS records still identify that address as QTS and no completion or transfer crosswalk was found, its planned investment, equipment and jobs are not treated as Meta Fort Worth observations.

research_updates.title: Metric disposition ledger — resources and community
research_updates.notes: study.annual_electricity_use is retained for 2020-2024. The 2024 observation supports three narrow syntheses: the EIA Texas 2024 industrial price is the central benchmark and the same-year commercial price is a separate class sensitivity after ERCOT/PUCT/Oncor review showed the actual retailer, voltage, class, demand and rider inputs are unavailable; deterministic leap-year average-load conversion; and an EPA eGRID ERCT-only location-based emissions point benchmark. The Texas state-output factor is production-geography context and is excluded from the Fort Worth consumption-region estimate and interval. These are not Meta's bill, peak demand, capacity, actual or market-based emissions. Actual 2020-2024 water withdrawal is preserved in an exact project-scoped catalog-and-claim proposal pending orchestrator catalog adoption; renewable capacity is statewide and excluded; generator runtime, fuel, demand, bills, wastewater and other resource costs remain unavailable. Community records retain nesting warnings; no complete recipient or annual giving ledger is claimed.
